doc.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Missing the Hopkins job; Benny Carter's 1941 band
summary: He did not get the Hopkins job but ended up in Benny Carter's 1941 band, who corrected his flat playing; he reflects on Sinatra.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Better than Satchmo. So anyway Edmond Hall said really? So anyway they sent for me to come up here. The bus fare was fifteen dollars from Pensacola, Florida to New York. It came. And when it came, for some reason I didn’t get the job. I’d been trying to say to myself, I’d played with him a couple of times, but I think there was another trumpet player named Louis Bacon that used to sing with Louis Armstrong. He was a ballad singer with Louis Armstrong. He got the job. But the next thing, I wound up with one of the greatest bands in the country, and I say this and God bless this man, he’s still alive, he’s 97 years old, but I was with the great Benny Carter band of 1941. And I guess you know, you’ve heard those records that were maybe twenty, twenty-five years ahead of the time. We recorded “I Surrender Dear” with him on trumpet. As a matter of fact Benny was one of the great trumpets, and is now, he’s one of the great trumpet players of our time. He taught me a lot of things. I remember I had a fault of playing a little flat you know. And when I joined the band he told me to my face he says, “You’re playing a little flat” he says, “I’ll straighten that out.” And he gave me a trumpet lick. Then that was it. And I haven’t seen this man in many, many years. Incidentally, I know all these things like this because I’ll tell you, in two weeks I will be 83 years old.

I will be 83 years old and one of the things, I’m just a little sad right now, because I knew Frank Sinatra, and not really, who knew Frankie? Not really, but I’ll tell you something, I hadn’t seen him but once in fifty years, can you imagine that? And I’ve been everywhere. Every place he went, we went, because you know the Erskine Hawkins band, we went everywhere.
